note: Human-readable labels and localized text patterns. collect.ps1 itself is pure ASCII; every non-ASCII string lives in these files and is read with an explicit UTF-8 decoder. t23 added patterns.serve_proxy_target and reason.serve_port_mismatch / reason.rem_serve_443 (paired in labels.zh.json), and reworded reason.serve_ok / reason.serve_unknown to the serve-target semantics.

exit.exit_0: safe/pass: every judgement passed - no unknown, no degraded, no blocked
exit.exit_1: degraded: at least one degraded and/or unknown item; the link may work but nothing unproven counts as good
exit.exit_2: blocked/unusable: at least one blocked item, or the collector itself could not run (missing fixture, unusable probes, refused -Apply)

manual.manual_s0_network: MANUAL: read the S0 paragraph of powercfg /a (a phrase like 'network disconnected' means entering S0 drops the network). This check only reports whether S0 exists plus the raw line.
manual.manual_serve_status: MANUAL: run 'tailscale serve status' in an ordinary (non-sandboxed) window and confirm the proxy target is 127.0.0.1:<dsh port> with --bg enabled.
manual.manual_https: MANUAL: an HTTPS/certificate verdict needs a client-side Node/OpenSSL probe (curl under schannel fails falsely). See raw.manualCommand.

title.wildcard_listener_inventory: Non-loopback listener inventory (stated separately from the DSH port)
title.trusted_hosts_patch: trustedHosts in the actually loaded patch
title.serve_present: serve listener on the tailnet side (443)
title.no_new_wildcard_listener: Read-only self-proof: no new wildcard listener

reason.os_ok: Authoritative registry values: branch {0}, build {1}.{2} (branch is decided by CurrentBuild: >=22000 is Win11; ProductName still says 'Windows 10' on Win11 and must not be used).
reason.reg_unavailable: Registry key {0} could not be read ({1}) - not judged this run.
reason.ps_ok: PowerShell {0}, execution policy {1}; this collector uses PS 5.1 syntax only and needs no pwsh 7, curl, CIM or node.
reason.ps_old: PowerShell {0} is older than 5.1 and this collector was never validated there - degraded.
reason.priv_ok: elevated={0}. Without elevation Get-NetFirewallRule / Get-NetConnectionProfile / powercfg /requests are unusable; this collector does not depend on them.
reason.tailnet_ok: Tailscale address(es) found: {0} (100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 are the ranges Tailscale uses).
reason.tailnet_unknown: No 100.64.0.0/10 or fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 address in the netsh address table or in the netstat listeners - possibly signed out, disconnected, or a different output shape. Not judged.
reason.netstat_unavailable: netstat probe unavailable ({0}) - every listener-related judgement is impossible.
reason.dsh_loopback_ok: Port {0}: all {1} LISTENING rows bind 127.0.0.1, and wildcard/other-interface hits are 0 - loopback exclusivity holds.
reason.dsh_exposed: The DSH port is bound to a non-loopback address: {0} - this breaks the core security premise of the whole setup.
reason.dsh_no_listener: Nothing listens on {0} and no DSH-owned loopback listener was found, so exclusivity cannot be judged (DSH may simply not be running).
reason.inv_dsh_exposed: A DSH process is listening on a non-loopback address: {0}.
reason.inv_ok: {0} non-loopback listeners, of which {1} are wildcard (0.0.0.0 / [::]). See raw.inventory. These are OTHER services on this machine (RDP/SMB/NetBIOS/third-party) and must be stated separately from the DSH-port statement.
reason.ts_not_installed: tailscale.exe was not auto-discovered (tried parameter, registry install dir, Program Files, LOCALAPPDATA, PATH) - prerequisite missing.
reason.ts_cli_ok: tailscale ip -4 exited 0 (version exit {0}, serve status exit {1}) - the CLI really is usable. A lone 'version' exit 0 is never proof.
reason.ts_pipe_denied: The tailscale CLI is refused by the named-pipe sandbox (exit {0}; text contains ProtectedPrefix\Administrators\Tailscale\tailscaled: Access is denied). This is a PROBE UNAVAILABLE, not 'not signed in', not 'serve missing'. Re-run in an ordinary (non-sandboxed) window.
reason.ts_not_logged_in: The tailscale CLI reports not signed in / not running: {0} - prerequisite missing.
reason.ts_probe_failed: The tailscale CLI probe failed (exit {0}) - not judged, raw text is in raw.
reason.ts_service_missing: No service named Tailscale - prerequisite missing (not installed).
reason.ts_service_stopped: Tailscale service exists but is {0} - the link is down.
reason.edge_ok: Stored registry value for Tailscale-Process is Edge=TRUE (matches the netsh echo '{0}') - Edge traversal has not been reverted. Note this is the PROCESS-level rule.
reason.edge_false: Stored registry value for Tailscale-Process is Edge=FALSE - Edge traversal has been reverted (or the rule was recreated). This is exactly the drift seen before.
reason.edge_rule_missing: No firewall rule named Tailscale-Process in the rule store - Tailscale is not installed, or the rule was deleted.
reason.edge_registry_unavailable: The firewall rule store registry key is unreadable ({0}); the netsh echo alone cannot prove drift (echo != stored value has happened here) - not judged.
reason.edge_value_unrecognized: Edge value {0} for Tailscale-Process is neither TRUE nor FALSE - not judged, no guessing.
reason.ts_in_ok: {0} Tailscale-In rules: address-level allows (LA4/LA6) covering Domain,Private with Edge=No (these two are SUPPOSED to be No; they are not the rule to inspect for drift).
reason.ts_in_missing: No Tailscale-In rule found; the built-in inbound allow is missing and a narrow allow is required (tailnet range only, tcp 443).
reason.ts_in_partial: Tailscale-In rules are incomplete (IPv4 present={0}, IPv6 present={1}); whichever half is missing keeps those clients out.
reason.ts_in_profile_narrow: Tailscale-In profiles are {0} and do not include Domain/Private, so these rules never apply.
reason.fw_registry_unavailable: The firewall rule store registry key is unreadable ({0}) - not judged.
reason.nic_ok: The Tailscale adapter sits in the {0} profile (source: {1}), so the built-in Tailscale-In allow applies.
reason.nic_public: The Tailscale adapter sits in the PUBLIC profile (source: {0}). Tailscale-In covers only Domain and Private, so those inbound allows silently stop working while serve/tailscale look perfectly healthy.
reason.nic_unparsed: The netsh output sections could not be mapped to profile names (structure parsed={0}, Get-NetConnectionProfile available={1}) - not judged; raw.netshRawOutput holds the original text for a human.
reason.nic_probe_failed: All adapter-profile probes are unusable ({0}) - not judged.
reason.fw_ok: Firewall is enabled for all three profiles (registry EnableFirewall=1; netsh parse saw {0} sections) - baseline holds.
reason.fw_partial_off: The firewall is OFF for: {0} - the inbound blocking surface is incomplete.
reason.fw_unavailable: Neither the registry nor netsh would report firewall state ({0}) - not judged.
reason.power_ok: STANDBYIDLE AC={0} / DC={1}: both are 0 = never idle-sleep, so the power policy cannot kill the link.
reason.power_dc_only: STANDBYIDLE DC={1} = {0} s: AC is 0 but the machine WILL sleep on battery. The honest wording is 'the link dies {0} s after mains power is lost', never a blanket 'sleep is disabled'.
reason.power_ac_nonzero: STANDBYIDLE AC={1} = {0} s: the machine sleeps on mains power too, so the server takes its own link down.
reason.power_unparsed: The powercfg output does not match the known template ({0}) and the alias cross-check disagreed, so no number is guessed. raw.allHex lists every 0x token.
reason.s0_ok: powercfg /a structure parsed: S0 available = {0} (first block lists available states, second lists unavailable ones). Whether entering S0 drops the network must be read from the raw line - see manual.
reason.s0_unparsed: powercfg /a does not match the template ({0} header lines) - not judged.
reason.exposure_ok: DSH networkExposure=loopback (mode={0}). This value only selects the HTTPS edge intent; the desktop web server host is hard-wired to 127.0.0.1.
reason.exposure_lan: DSH networkExposure={0} - different from the loopback default; confirm it is intentional. The host stays 127.0.0.1 but the exposure intent changes.
reason.exposure_key_absent: settings.yaml exists but has no networkExposure key; the default would apply, but this collector will not present a default as a measured value.
reason.th_ok: trustedHosts in the actually loaded patch matches the tailnet name: {0} - remote /api calls will not be fenced with 403.
reason.th_blocked: {0} trustedHosts keys exist in the actually loaded patch, but none matches the tailnet name (the common shape is 'trustedHosts: []'). The remote UI opens while every /api call is answered 403, which the client shows as an endless 'reconnecting'.
reason.th_unavailable: No cordis patch file could be read ({0}) - not judged.
reason.th_multi_profile: Several DSH profiles were found ({0}) and -Profile was not given, so this collector refuses to silently pick the first one - not judged. Re-run with -Profile <name>.
reason.th_key_absent: trustedHosts does not appear at all in the {0} patch files read, so the effective value cannot be determined - not guessed. A server-side deployment must set it explicitly.
reason.serve_ok: {0} listener(s) on 443 over a tailnet address, owned by tailscaled, and the readable serve status proxies to the measured DSH port - the serve entry point exists and points at the right place.
reason.serve_owner_other: 443 on the tailnet address is owned by a non-tailscaled process ({0}) - serve may not be effective, possible port conflict.
reason.serve_unknown: The serve target cannot be read: 'tailscale serve status' exited {0}, or its output names no proxy target. Without a readable target this check cannot tell 'serve is not configured' from 'tailscaled terminates TLS outside the Windows TCP stack', and the tailnet listener shape is NOT evidence (every connected node carries tailscaled-owned tailnet listeners) - not judged. Re-run serve status in an ordinary (non-sandboxed) window.
reason.serve_port_mismatch: tailscale serve is readable and proxies to 127.0.0.1:{0}, but the measured DSH port is {1} - the remote UI would reach a dead port and the narrow ACL (client -> server tcp:443) silently stops protecting anything.
reason.peer_not_provided: -Peer / -PeerName not supplied, so client-side link probes did not run - not judged.
reason.peer_443_ok: TCP handshake to the peer's 443 succeeded ({0} ms) - TCP-layer reachable (TCP only, no TLS/HTTP).
reason.peer_443_refused: The peer actively refused 443 ({0} ms) - path works but nothing listens on 443 (serve not running or wrong port).
reason.peer_443_timeout: Timed out after {0} ms (dropped, not refused) - packets are dropped by an ACL/firewall, or the peer is asleep. This is not an active refusal.
reason.peer_iso_ok: 135/5357 and the DSH port are all unreachable from the tailnet side - the narrow allow (443 only) holds.
reason.peer_iso_dsh_open: The peer's DSH port {0} is reachable from the tailnet - loopback exclusivity is broken or serve points at the wrong port. Serious.
reason.peer_iso_too_open: These non-443 ports are reachable from the tailnet: {0} - the ACL is wider than intended.
reason.dns_off_tailnet: {0} resolved to {1}, outside the tailnet range - possible DNS hijack/proxy rewrite, or the peer is in another tailnet.
reason.dns_hostnotfound: Name {0} does not resolve (HostNotFound) - misspelling, or the peer is not in this tailnet. Domain names must be resolved for real, never recalled from memory.
reason.dns_failed: DNS probe failed (result={0}, error={1}) - not judged.
reason.proxy_ok: System proxy is not in the way ({0}) - the browser will not bypass the direct path.
reason.proxy_hijack: A system proxy is enabled and the bypass list has no entry for {0} / 100.64.0.0/10 - the browser may time out while scripted probes succeed.
reason.https_client_only: An HTTPS/certificate verdict is impossible from PowerShell here (node availability: see raw.nodeAvailable); curl under schannel reports false failures. This check is permanently 'unknown' and ships the manual command instead.
reason.cred_ok: Self-audit clean: none of the executed probe command strings and none of the {0} file paths read show any access to a secret store.
reason.cred_violation: Self-audit found {0} suspected secret-store access(es) - stop and investigate immediately.
reason.ro_no_new_wildcard: Wildcard listeners: {0} before, {1} after collection, empty difference - this run added no 0.0.0.0/[::] listener.
reason.ro_new_wildcard: A wildcard listener appeared during collection: {0} - the read-only contract is violated, investigate immediately.
reason.ro_probe_unavailable: The before/after netstat snapshots were not both available, so the read-only self-proof cannot be made - not judged.
reason.rem_th_add: Add the server MagicDNS name to connection.trustedHosts in the active profile patch, then restart DSH from its own Restart menu (never a third-party restart plugin).
reason.rem_nic_private: Set the Tailscale network category back to Private, or add a narrow inbound allow for the tailnet (tcp 443 only, tailnet range only).
reason.rem_fw_on: Turn Windows Firewall back on for all profiles (netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state on).
reason.rem_power_ac: Set the AC idle-sleep timeout to 0 (powercfg /change standby-timeout-ac 0); a sleeping server kills the link.
reason.rem_power_dc: Set the DC idle-sleep timeout to 0 (powercfg /change standby-timeout-dc 0); otherwise the link dies once mains power is lost.
reason.rem_ts_install: Install Tailscale yourself with the official interactive MSI plus browser sign-in; this plugin never automates account sign-in.
reason.rem_edge_restore: Restore the Tailscale-Process rule (repair/reinstall Tailscale), then re-run this check; record the previous value first so the change is reversible.
reason.rem_dsh_exposed: Use netstat -ano to find the process that binds the DSH port to a non-loopback address and fix that process' own configuration; this collector changes nothing.
reason.rem_exposure_loopback: If LAN exposure was not intended, set dsh-desktop.networkExposure back to loopback and restart DSH from its own menu.
reason.rem_proxy_bypass: Add the tailnet name/range to the proxy bypass list, or disable the system proxy while using the link.
reason.rem_serve_443: Republish the DSH loopback port so serve proxies to it (tailscale serve --bg <dsh port>, published on 443); change the narrow ACL only if you really intend a different published port.
